pr_title: Editor: Fix escaping issues with POT generator
pr_body:
* Closes #80004.

**Note:** I'm not familiar with `gettext`, please test this if you are.

```gdscript
print(tr(""))
print(tr("\n"))
print(tr("Test 1."))
print(tr("Test 2.\n"))
print(tr("Test 3.\nNewline."))
print(tr("Test 4.\nNewline.\n"))
print(tr("Test 5. \\n - Not newline."))
print(tr("Test 6. \" \\"))
```

**Before:**

```pot
#: node.gd
msgid ""
msgstr ""

#: node.gd
msgid ""
"\n"
""
msgstr ""

#: node.gd
msgid "Test 1."
msgstr ""

#: node.gd
msgid ""
"Test 2.\n"
""
msgstr ""

#: node.gd
msgid ""
"Test 3.\n"
"Newline."
msgstr ""

#: node.gd
msgid ""
"Test 4.\n"
"Newline.\n"
""
msgstr ""

#: node.gd
msgid ""
"Test 5. \n"
" - Not newline."
msgstr ""

#: node.gd
msgid "Test 6. " \"
msgstr ""
```

**After:**

```pot
#: node.gd
msgid ""
msgstr ""

#: node.gd
msgid "\n"
msgstr ""

#: node.gd
msgid "Test 1."
msgstr ""

#: node.gd
msgid "Test 2.\n"
msgstr ""

#: node.gd
msgid ""
"Test 3.\n"
"Newline."
msgstr ""

#: node.gd
msgid ""
"Test 4.\n"
"Newline.\n"
msgstr ""

#: node.gd
msgid "Test 5. \\n - Not newline."
msgstr ""

#: node.gd
msgid "Test 6. \" \\"
msgstr ""
```
pr_comments:
> Escaping file paths looks unnecessary. But yeah, newlines in a path seem not forbidden :P

I just added protection in case the string had newlines for some reason. Because the comment ends on a newline.

issue_context.title: Impossible to generate well formated POT files when a `String` with `\"` is used
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v4.1.stable.official [970459615]

### System information

Godot v4.1.stable - Windows 10.0.22621 - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 (NVIDIA; 31.0.15.3667) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-8300H CPU @ 2.30GHz (8 Threads)

### Issue description

When generating a POT file using Godot Editor, if the `String` contains double quotes, its entry in the POT file will be wrong (see below).

### Steps to reproduce

Create this script:
```
extends Control


func _ready():
	
	var a: String = tr("\"Problematic\" string")
	print(a)
```

And then generate a POT file from it. You will get something like:
```
# LANGUAGE translation for Bugs for the following files:
# res://main.gd
#
# FIRST AUTHOR < EMAIL @ADDRESS>, YEAR.
#
#, fuzzy
msgid ""
msgstr ""
"Project-Id-Version: Bugs\n"
"MIME-Version: 1.0\n"
"Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8\n"
"Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8-bit\n"

#: main.gd
msgid ""Problematic" string"
msgstr ""
```

The problem cames from the extra double quotes inside the string, they will raise an error when generating a PO file.

A possible solution would be to make:
```
extends Control


func _ready():
	
	TranslationServer.set_locale("fr")
	var a: String = tr("\\\"Problematic\\\" string")
	print(a)
```

Therefore, the POT file:
```
# LANGUAGE translation for Bugs for the following files:
# res://main.gd
#
# FIRST AUTHOR < EMAIL @ADDRESS>, YEAR.
#
#, fuzzy
msgid ""
msgstr ""
"Project-Id-Version: Bugs\n"
"MIME-Version: 1.0\n"
"Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8\n"
"Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8-bit\n"

#: main.gd
msgid "\"Problematic\" string"
msgstr ""
```

But then, the string is not recognized. This is the PO file with an extra entry added manually:
```
# LANGUAGE translation for Bugs for the following files:
# res://main.gd
#
# FIRST AUTHOR < EMAIL @ADDRESS>, 2023.
#
msgid ""
msgstr ""
"Project-Id-Version: Bugs\n"
"MIME-Version: 1.0\n"
"Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8\n"
"Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit\n"
"Last-Translator: Automatically generated\n"
"Language-Team: none\n"
"Language: fr\n"
"Plural-Forms: nplurals=2; plural=(n > 1);\n"

#: main.gd
msgid "\"Problematic\" string"
msgstr "TEST0"

msgid "\\\"Problematic\\\" string"
msgstr "TEST1"
```
Then `print(a)` prints `TEST1` instead of `TEST0`.

### Minimal reproduction project

[project.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/12207357/project.zip)

review_comments: Style-wise this could probably be on the same line.
Sorry if the displayed diff makes it confusing. I mean that the entire project id thing can be on the same line, instead of being 3 lines.

Do you mean like this:

```c++
			"\"Project-Id-Version: " + project_name +
			"\\n\"\n"
			"\"MIME-Version: 1.0\\n\"\n"
			"\"Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8\\n\"\n"
			"\"Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8-bit\\n\"\n";
```

Or should I revert this part?

`clang-format` requires string literal concatenation (without the `+` operator) to continue in the same column as previous literal.

```c++
			"\"Project-Id-Version: " + project_name + "\\n\"\n"
								  "\"MIME-Version: 1.0\\n\"\n"
								  "\"Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8\\n\"\n"
								  "\"Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8-bit\\n\"\n";
```

(GitHub displays tabs as 8 spaces in comments, so I changed the actual requirement for clarity.)
Ah, that's why it was like that before. Damn, that sucks. I guess the first line works without triggering clang-format because the next line is a variable, not a literal? And thus it uses `+`.
